svg.title: State space models: the recurrence unrolled, where the selective parameters come from, and the parallel scan that trains it
svg.text: State space models, one token at a time
S4 gave the recurrence, Mamba made it depend on the token, and a parallel scan made it trainable.
THE RECURRENCE, WHAT RUNS AT INFERENCE
Three moves per token. Fade what is already stored, write the new token into it, read one output back out. The state never changes size.
The memory is those six numbers, and it is still six numbers at token 4 or at token 40 000. Constant memory, finite capacity, that is the entire trade.
WHERE Aₜ, Bₜ AND Cₜ COME FROM, AND WHY MAMBA CHANGED IT
S4 learned one A, one B, one C and reused them for every token. Mamba computes a fresh set from the token itself, which is what lets it skip filler.
S4, one fixed set for all t, a convolution
Mamba, a new set per token, selective
Cₜ goes straight to the read
WHAT THE STEP SIZE Δₜ ACTUALLY DOES
Δₜ large, a token worth remembering
Aₜ = exp(Δₜ · A) collapses toward 0, so the stored state fades fast and Bₜ·xₜ
writes the new token in. The memory moves.
Δₜ near zero, filler or punctuation
Aₜ goes to 1 and Bₜ goes to 0, so the previous state passes through untouched
and the token is skipped. That is selectivity, in one number.
Making A depend on the token breaks the convolution S4 trained with, which is why Mamba needed a scan kernel that keeps h in SRAM and never writes it to HBM.
WHY IT TRAINS AS FAST AS A TRANSFORMER, THE PARALLEL SCAN
The update is affine in h, so two consecutive steps merge into a single equivalent step. The chain becomes a tree, and the tree fits a GPU.
Sequential, what the inference loop does
8 tokens, 8 dependent steps. The depth grows with the sequence and the GPU waits.
The merge operator, associative, which is what makes the tree legal
Parallel scan, exactly the same result
THE LINE, WHAT EACH STEP ACTUALLY CHANGED
one fixed A, B, C, a long convolution
A, B, C read off the token, plus a scan
the same object as linear attention
complex state, half the decoding cost
